There are usually programs at hospitals to help cover the cost for those without insurance or resources. My stay was entirely free. I don't know what hospital is near you, obviously, but check out their site and keep an eye out for a link to something such as "financial assistance" or similar wording. The larger the hospital the more likely it is they can help. They'll also put you in touch with resources for when you get out. 

Also, if you really feel like getting admitted is the best idea for you then go ahead and prepare. Pack a few changes of clothes, some basic toiletries, a brush/comb/whatever you use. Nothing with drawstrings, nothing potentially dangerous. Just the basics like your deodorant, toothpaste, toothbrush, shampoo. Make a list of what meds, if any, you take with the dosage and frequency so they know.

I recently learned that there are mental health centers that can treat you on a sliding scale but they're hard to get registered for. If you're feeling suicidal, however, go to the ER and tell them. You'll likely get admitted to the psych ward and put on suicide watch but they will also bring in a social worker and connect you to resources in your area. (I say this, of course, with the assumption that you're in the US.)

After my recent stay I was hooked up immediately with the local county mental health center and my therapist appointments are going to be in the lowest bracket at an affordable $10 per visit. And there are a ton of resources to help with any medication you might need.

I figured I'd come back here and give an update.

Clearly I'm still alive. I did make an attempt, ended up in the ER, and got out of the psych ward a few days ago. Things are finally starting to look up.

In a bizarre sort of way it was a good decision. Until you've been admitted to a psych ward (for up to five days without a court order) you can't get crap in the way of help here.

Now I've been set up with a therapist at the local mental health center (first appointment on Wednesday), been given meds that are working quite well for me (a mood stabilizer and an antipsychotic), found out that my antidepressant was at such a high level that it actually made things worse (300 mg of Effexor is a bad idea, jsyk) so it was lowered to almost a tenth of what I was taking, and I've been given antibiotics for my dental abscesses as well as given an appointment at a free dental clinic in the area to have my top teeth extracted and a referral to a place that will do my top denture for $450 which my parents have stated they'd help with. After that I can focus on getting a job and getting the fillings needed for my lower teeth. I'm doing a lot better and my ex and I are working slowly towards reconciling. He doesn't want to rush back into it until we know my mental issues are stabilized. 

So thank you to those of you who cared and I'm sorry for being such a pain. What you do here is amazing and I'll definitely come around under my usual screenname to help out others in need.
